resources.title: FCE360 Enhanced
resources.author: frankischilling · original FCE360 / FCEUX contributors
resources.description: NES / Famicom emulator with ROM search, favorites, rewind, save states and Lua scripting.
resources.prerequisites: Your own .nes or .zip ROMs in roms\. Keep the full media folder, including ui.xzp and xarialuni.ttf, beside fceux.xex. Famicom Disk System use additionally needs your own matching BIOS.
resources.runtime: RGH/JTAG Xbox 360, explicitly targeted by the author. No exact motherboard or minimum dashboard version is published.
resources.temporary: The author targets RGH/JTAG; BadUpdate, ABadAvatar and Peer Pressure are not separately certified. Release 0.8.10 still lists Xbox 360 timing/gameplay testing as outstanding.
setup: Extract the complete release and put its XEX and media directory together in the shown FCEUX360 folder. Check the archive wrapper before copying, so the XEX is directly inside the final folder.
Put your own .nes / .zip files in roms\ and launch fceux.xex from Aurora, FSD or XeXMenu.
Keep fceui.ini, scripts, ROMs, BIOS, screenshots, saves and states when upgrading. Battery saves use sav\; screenshots use snaps\.
resources.notes: START + BACK opens the in-game menu; LT rewinds, RT fast-forwards and right-stick click captures a screenshot. Use the full ZIP for a new installation; the standalone XEX asset alone omits required media.
resources.imageCredit: frankischilling · official FCE360 Enhanced recent-games screenshot

resources.title: Salvia 360
resources.author: danibiker · libretro core contributors
resources.description: Native libretro frontend for Nintendo, Sega, PlayStation, arcade and computer systems, with per-core settings and RetroAchievements.
resources.prerequisites: Your own games in the appropriate Roms system subfolders and any required personal BIOS files in system\. Keep all bundled cores, configurations and supporting assets together; Xbox 360 and Windows releases are distinct downloads.
resources.runtime: Homebrew-enabled Xbox 360 capable of unsigned XEX loading. The base frontend does not publish an exact minimum dashboard or motherboard list. Optional USB mouse support specifically needs kernel 17559 and a DashLaunch plugin.
resources.temporary: No specific temporary-exploit combination is certified in the frontend documentation. The optional hidmouse.xex DashLaunch plugin is a separate setup and must not be assumed compatible with Peer Pressure or another runtime without plugin support.
resources.launch: Confirm launcher filename from the verified release ZIP before publishing
setup: Extract the complete Xbox 360 release into a dedicated Salvia folder on HDD or USB; the author suggests Usb0:\Salvia. Keep all core XEX files and their supporting directories together.

Keep Roms next to the XEX files or at the USB root. Put personal games into their system subfolders, such as nes, snes, Genesis, gb, gba, n64, psx and fbneo. Supply only BIOS files needed by the cores you use.

Change the library parent directory in Options → Emulation → Roms Main Directory, or roms_path in salvia.cfg. The frontend uses Hdd:\ for internal-HDD game paths and usb:\ to detect the USB port automatically.
resources.notes: SELECT + START exits emulation and SELECT + Y toggles the options menu by default. Saves/states are under data\saves and data\states. N64 support improved in 1.1.0; game compatibility remains core-specific. Mouse support is optional, not a requirement for controller use.

resources.title: Simple 360 Player
resources.author: HG-ERIK · FFmpeg / FFPlay360 contributors
resources.description: Local media player with subtitle and audio-track selection for videos on HDD, USB or disc.
resources.prerequisites: Supported personal media files. H.264 up to 720p, Xvid/DivX, MPEG-2 and WMV/VC-1 are supported; H.265/HEVC, VP8/VP9 and AV1 are unsupported. Keep the complete release folder.
resources.runtime: RGH/JTAG Xbox 360, explicitly specified by the author. Launch through Aurora, FSD or XeXMenu. No exact motherboard or dashboard build is pinned.
resources.temporary: BadUpdate, ABadAvatar and Peer Pressure are not separately certified by this app’s documentation.
setup: Extract the ZIP on your PC and copy the whole Simple360Player folder into Apps on the console’s HDD or USB drive.
Launch default.xex from Aurora, FSD or XeXMenu and browse your own videos. Matching external .srt subtitles stay beside the video file.
Keep settings.ini when upgrading. The app writes settings and a log only beside its executable.
resources.notes: Press X during playback for aspect ratio and Y for audio/subtitle/options controls. 1080p H.264 is too demanding according to the author. Surround passthrough was not physically tested by this site.
resources.imageCredit: HG-ERIK · official Simple 360 Player file-browser screenshot

resources.title: Multiplex 360
resources.author: HG-ERIK · FFmpeg / FFPlay360 contributors
resources.description: Unofficial Plex client with server libraries, profiles, subtitles and playback resume.
resources.prerequisites: Network access, your Plex account and an accessible Plex server/library. H.264 up to 720p can play directly; the Plex server transcodes other formats. Keep the entire app folder writable.
resources.runtime: RGH / JTAG / BadUpdate Xbox 360, all explicitly named by the author. No exact motherboard or dashboard requirement is specified by the app; the BadUpdate entry point itself requires dashboard 17559.
resources.temporary: BadUpdate is explicitly supported. Re-establish its temporary unsigned-code session after reboot. ABadAvatar and Peer Pressure are not separately certified in the app documentation.
setup: Extract the release ZIP and copy its complete Multiplex360 folder to HDD or USB; start default.xex through your existing homebrew dashboard.
On first launch the console displays a code. Enter it at plex.tv/link on your phone or PC and select your Plex profile.
Keep auth.ini and settings when upgrading. From version 0.4 the app asks before installing its own updates and preserves the previous executable as default.old.
resources.notes: The author states it works with DashLaunch liveblock enabled and needs neither Xbox Live nor a stealth server. It writes only inside its own folder. Sign out through Settings or remove auth.ini yourself.

resources.title: Silverdash360
resources.author: jessenic / Digiex
resources.description: Silverlight-based dashboard with game/app shelves, box art, local and DLNA media, file browser and FTP.
resources.prerequisites: The complete console base package plus the 0.1.3 update below. The small GitHub update is not a standalone installation. Keep a way to return to your existing dashboard.
resources.runtime: RGH/JTAG Xbox 360, explicitly required by the official installation guide. The app is not signed for a stock retail console; no exact dashboard or motherboard revision is stated.
resources.temporary: BadUpdate, ABadAvatar and Peer Pressure are not separately certified by the author. Do not infer support merely because another dashboard launches in that runtime.
setup: Extract Silverdash360-0.1.2-console.zip. It contains the complete Silverdash360 folder and required runtime files.
Extract the 0.1.3 update into that Silverdash360 folder on your PC, applying the new files there. Preserve both original archives and a copy of your existing installation.
Copy the prepared Silverdash360 folder into Apps on HDD or USB, then start default.xex. Review the first-run FTP settings; the first library scan may take time.
Keep the Data folder beside default.xex when upgrading: it holds settings, library data and cached artwork.
